newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up on aggressive RBI dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up on aggressive RBI dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.8050/8150 after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened aggressively on Monday to arrest the rupee's rise, dealers said.
Spot rupee opened steady at 35.78/79 and was mostly firm until noon in the absence of major demand.
As an expected dollar demand from the RBI did not take place until early afternoon, the rupee started rising, touching a high of 35.77, triggering RBI action, dealers said.
The RBI started buying in lots of $5.0 million at 35.78 and continued its buying upto the 35.80 level, dealers said.
"It was aggressive and they must have bought a large amount today," said a dealer.
"RBI's action was better today (compared to its dollar buying in recent days)," said a dealer. "The market was caught short and rupee touched 35.810 because of short-covering."
Towards the close, dollar demand from cities outside Bombay pushed down the rupee to the day's low of 35.815, a dealer at a state-run bank said.
RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told the Indian Merchants Chamber on Monday the central bank sought to arrest the appreciation of the rupee and to keep the exchange rate "fairly stable."

He said RBI wanted a proper integration of the forex and money markets and and sought to achieve the twin objectives of inflation control and a competitive exchange rate through its day-to-day operations.
Forward dollar premiums continued to soften as exporters, resigned to a strong rupee, continued to sell their dollar receivables, a dealer said.
The six month annualised forward premium fell to 4.36 percent compared to the previous close of 4.47 percent.
"Premiums may go down to 4.25 percent but that may be the bottom for now," said a dealer.
"A government auction may appear next week and there would be tax outflows (from the banking system) on June 15," he said.
"But after all is said and done, the upside is absolutely limited, and 4.8/4.9 percent should be a safe cap."
